claims.text: An enhanced-sampling free-energy algorithm can explicitly integrate the melting transition pathway.
The proposed algorithm can accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-induced volume change across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The proposed algorithm can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The target initial state is a chemically disordered, near-equiatomic HEA solid below its melting temperature.
Directly probing the melting pathway captures both kinetic and thermodynamic details of melting.
The simulations can be conducted under conditions that mimic experimental heating.
Atomic rearrangements and events such as surface premelting or phase separation mediate the solid-to-liquid transformation in HEAs.
Statistical-mechanical free-energy techniques overcome kinetic barriers along the melting pathway.
Free-energy calculations can separate and quantify intrinsic enthalpic and entropic contributions at finite temperature.
Integrating the melting pathway enables precise calculation of melting properties and associated volume changes.
Predicted melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting-volume change will be within approximately 5–10% of experimental benchmarks.
The method will reliably characterize liquid-phase thermodynamics across a diverse set of HEAs.
Traditional calorimetry, differential thermal analysis, and conventional simulations are less efficient or less accurate over the full HEA compositional range.
The approach will work best for near-equiatomic compositions having disordered solid solutions.
Extreme non-ideal interactions or strong long-range ordering may limit the approach.
Quantitative accuracy and computational efficiency across the full HEA compositional space remain unvalidated.
Subtle phase behavior or kinetic hindrances not overcome by enhanced sampling could cause deviations.
Systematic deviations greater than approximately 10% from experimental benchmarks across multiple HEAs would falsify the proposed methodology.
Failure of the computed free-energy profiles to reveal a clear melting-transition pathway would falsify the proposed methodology.
